reasons.reader_question: Clear twin question: will reading the writ cost the spears and the pass, and will Neela say what she is at the gate?
reasons.change: Both temptations are now spoken and Devan commits to reading the writ. The split of roles mostly repeats ch20's terms (F907).
reasons.romance_movement: Being seen becomes something she asks for with the lamp lit. That reason is new. 'Won't speak for her' repeats ch20.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Thumb on the blister, the stitches kissed past, and the shared ache under her arm all show attraction through response, not narration.
reasons.character_logic: Devan's cost-count is sharp. He has used this hollow repeatedly, yet 'never found' a scrap under the camphor block, which strains belief.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Cost is named exactly: spears, pass, garrison trust, and the 'not knowing' Devan agrees to carry.
reasons.prose: Clean and concrete. 'Rough/roughly' repeats, the sex scene has generic patches, the count speech is clunky, and the pebble ending is redundant.
reasons.continuity: Draft says chit and seal stayed in the hollow and only the writ travelled. F744/F916 put chit and writ, then seal, in his pack on the hill.

fixes: At 'There was room for a third thing, and the third thing was not there' there is a continuity conflict with F744/F916. Follow the beat: Devan returned the whole oilcloth bundle to the hollow last night (F910), so at dawn she finds chit, writ and seal together. Cut the 'Since the hill' exchange. Keep him lifting the writ and declaring he will read it.

At 'A scrap of paper, folded twice, gone soft as cloth' the setup is unfair and the image is recycled from Asha's chest (F418). Replace it with Devan taking Asha's real last note from his carved box (F415) and reading the full line he withheld in book 1, 'If you're reading this, I was right...'. That makes it a true rung on the disclosure ladder, not a convenient discovery.

At 'I won't take the command,' she said. 'That's settled.' the beat wants the explicit scene to change the bargain. Move this decision to after the lovemaking, prompted by being seen. Cut the redundant 'And not put it in your mouth.' Restate the count as 'A hundred and four. Six in the ground. Ninety-eight.' Change one of the two 'roughly' lines.
reader_question: When Devan reads the queen's writ aloud at the gate with three hundred of her spears watching, will it break the defence of the pass, and will Neela name herself there?
new_facts_assessment: F1036 conflicts with on-page ch2 (F744: chit and writ both in his pack) and with F916, F927 and F1015, and it contradicts the beat. F1037 recycles F115/F418 (the 'Say it anyway' line under a camphor block), is implausible, and is unnecessary. F1038 is consistent and useful.
